examples.en: I found a shelter to get out of the rain.
The hut in the mountains became our refuge.
This library is a refuge for my mind.
When a typhoon comes, the school is used as a shelter.
The nearest shelter is the gym.
We spent one night at the shelter.

explain: 위험을 피해 가는 곳이 '피난처'예요. 재난 안내문에서는 '대피소'라는 말도 자주 보여요. 몸이 아니라 마음이 쉬는 곳을 '마음의 피난처'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: It suddenly rained, so I looked for shelter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험이나 나쁜 날씨를 피할 곳을 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking for a place to escape danger or bad weather.

phrases.en: This café is my emotional refuge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아니라 마음이 쉬는 곳을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for a place where the heart can rest.

phrases.en: Please move to the nearest shelter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재난 안내문에서 자주 보이는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word often seen in disaster notices.

explain_en: A place you go to escape danger is a 피난처. On disaster notices you will also see the word 대피소. It can also be a place where the mind finds rest, as in '마음의 피난처'.

t90.ax: The nearest shelter is the gym.

examples.en: In the movie, a pirate ship sailed over the sea.
The amusement park has a pirate-ship-shaped ride.
The kids collected boxes, saying they would build a pirate ship.
The pirate ship flag has a skull drawn on it.

examples.ko: 저는 해적선에서 보물을 찾는 게임을 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like games where you search for treasure on a pirate ship.
I heard an old pirate ship was found under the sea.

explain: '선'은 배를 뜻하는 한자라서 '유람선', '여객선', '어선'처럼 여러 단어 끝에 붙어요. 혼자 '선'이라고는 안 하고 '배'라고 해요. 발음은 [해적썬]으로 '선'이 된소리가 돼요.

phrases.en: I rode the pirate ship at the amusement park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배나 놀이기구를 탈 때 '타다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 타다 for riding a ship or ride.

phrases.en: The pirate ship captain hid the treasure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기나 영화에 나오는 배의 우두머리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the captain in stories or movies.

phrases.en: The child's bed in the room is shaped like a pirate ship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 모습이 해적선 같을 때 '모양'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 모양 when something looks like a pirate ship.

explain_en: '선' is a Sino-Korean character meaning ship and ends words like '유람선', '여객선' and '어선'. By itself you say '배', not '선'. It is pronounced [해적썬], with a tensed '선'.

examples.ko: 여행을 안 간 게 두고두고 후회로 남았어요.
examples.en: Not going on the trip remained a regret for a long time.

examples.ko: 친구는 밥을 한 번 사 놓고 두고두고 생색을 내요.
examples.en: My friend bought me a meal once and keeps bragging about it forever.

examples.ko: 이 멸치볶음은 두고두고 먹을 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like this stir-fried anchovy side dish because I can eat it over a long time.

examples.ko: 선생님이 해 주신 말씀은 두고두고 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: What my teacher said to me stays in my memory for a long time.

examples.ko: 그 일은 두고두고 이야기할 만큼 웃겼어요.
examples.en: That incident was funny enough to talk about again and again.

examples.ko: 선물 받은 책을 두고두고 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm reading the book I got as a gift little by little, again and again.

explain: '오래오래'와 비슷하지만 한 번 있었던 일을 시간이 지나도 계속 떠올리거나 말할 때 많이 써요. '후회, 기억, 이야기'와 자주 어울려요. 음식이나 물건을 아껴서 오래 쓸 때도 '두고두고 먹다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 그때 사과하지 않은 걸 두고두고 후회해요.
phrases.en: I regret not apologizing then, again and again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일을 시간이 지나도 계속 아쉬워할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for regretting a past event long afterward.

phrases.example: 김치를 많이 담가서 두고두고 먹을 거예요.
phrases.en: I made a lot of kimchi, so I'll eat it for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 아껴서 오랫동안 나눠 먹는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making food last by eating it little by little over a long time.
phrases.en_equiv: eat little by little over time

phrases.example: 친구가 해 준 말을 두고두고 기억할 거예요.
phrases.en: I'll remember what my friend said for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고마움이나 감동이 오래 남을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when gratitude or being moved stays with you for a long time.

explain_en: It is similar to '오래오래' (for a long time), but it is often used when you keep recalling or talking about something that happened once. It goes well with words like regret, memory and story. It is also used for making food or things last, as in '두고두고 먹다'.

examples.ko: 그 친구를 영영 못 볼까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried I may never see that friend again.
I never found the ring I lost.

examples.ko: 그는 고향을 떠나 영영 돌아오지 않았어요.
examples.en: He left his hometown and never came back.

examples.ko: 이러다가 영영 한국어를 못 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: At this rate, I feel I'll never speak Korean.

examples.ko: 영영 안 올 줄 알았는데 왔네요.
examples.en: I thought he'd never come, but he did.
That letter was never delivered.

explain: 거의 항상 '못', '안', '없다'처럼 부정하는 말과 같이 써서 '다시는 ~하지 않는다'는 느낌이에요. '영원히'는 좋은 뜻에도 쓰지만 '영영'은 아쉽고 슬픈 상황에 잘 써요. '영영 잊지 못하다'처럼 감정이 강할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 집을 나간 고양이가 영영 돌아오지 않았어요.
phrases.en: The cat that left home never came back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영영' 뒤에는 부정하는 말이 와서 아쉬운 마음을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '영영' is followed by a negative and shows a sense of regret.

phrases.en: I never found out the reason.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝까지 알지 못했다는 아쉬움이 들어 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries the feeling of regret that one never found out.

phrases.en: I won't be late ever again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영영'은 아쉬움에 쓰고, '다시는'은 다짐이나 약속에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '영영' expresses regret, while '다시는' is often used for promises and resolutions.

explain_en: It nearly always pairs with a negative such as 못, 안, or 없다, giving the sense of never again. 영원히 can be used for happy things, but 영영 leans toward regret or sadness. It fits emotional lines like 영영 잊지 못하다 (can never forget).

t90.ax: I never found the ring I lost.

examples.en: My grandfather farmed all his life.
She lived with books her whole life.
In my whole life, I have never had food this good.
He donated the money he had saved over a lifetime to a school.

examples.ko: 저는 일평생 이 동네를 떠난 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never left this town in my entire life.

examples.ko: 일평생 후회하지 않을 선택을 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to make a choice I will never regret in my life.

explain: '평생'과 거의 같지만 '일평생'은 좀 더 힘주어 말하거나 글에서 쓰는 느낌이 있어요. 대화에서는 '평생'이 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요. 보통 '일평생 ~만 하다'처럼 부사처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I have lived in this neighborhood all my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일평생'보다 대화에서 더 자연스럽고 편하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more natural and casual in conversation than the headword.

phrases.en: My grandmother lived for her family her whole life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 오랜 삶을 돌아보는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but with a feeling of looking back on a long life.

phrases.en: He devoted his whole life to research.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일에 삶 전체를 쓸 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when giving one's entire life to one thing.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '평생', but '일평생' sounds a bit more emphatic or written. In conversation '평생' is often more natural. It is usually used like an adverb, as in '일평생 ~만 하다'.

examples.en: We have no time, so let's leave without delay.
Traffic was bad and I was delayed by a whole hour.

examples.ko: 지체할 시간이 없어서 바로 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: There was no time to waste, so I went straight to the hospital.

examples.ko: 세금 내는 일을 지체하면 벌금이 나올 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you put off paying your taxes, you may be fined.
He lingered on the road and missed the bus.
I'm really sorry for being slow to reply.

explain: 지체하다는 해야 할 일을 빨리 하지 않고 시간을 끌 때 써요. '지체하지 말고 ~하세요'처럼 서두르라고 재촉할 때 가장 자주 나와요. '늦다'는 정해진 시간을 넘긴 것이고, 지체하다는 그 사이 머뭇거리거나 시간을 끈다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: When you get the call, come without delay.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바로, 곧'이라는 뜻으로 급할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means 'right away'; used when something is urgent.

phrases.en: Don't delay. The door will close soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서두르라고 재촉하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A way to urge someone to hurry.

phrases.en: Delivery is being delayed because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 자연스럽게 늦어지는 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something ends up delayed by circumstances.

explain_en: 지체하다 is used when you put off something that should be done quickly and let time slip. It appears most in urging phrases like '지체하지 말고 ~하세요'. '늦다' is about passing a set time, while 지체하다 feels like dawdling in between.

t90.ax: I'm really sorry for being slow to reply.

examples.ko: 타임머신이 있다면 과거로 가 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: If there were a time machine, I would like to go to the past.

examples.ko: 영화에서 주인공이 타임머신을 타고 미래로 갔어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the hero rode a time machine to the future.

examples.ko: 타임머신 같은 건 현실에는 아직 없어요.
examples.en: Things like time machines don't exist in reality yet.
I want to go back to my childhood by time machine.
My friend lent me a book about time machines.
We don't even have a time machine, so how can we go back to yesterday?

explain: '타임머신을 타다'처럼 '타다'와 함께 써요. 오래된 물건이나 사진을 보고 옛날로 돌아간 느낌이 들면 '타임머신을 탄 것 같아요'라고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 타임머신을 타고 옛날로 가 보고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to ride a time machine and go back to the old days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탈것이기 때문에 '타다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because it is a vehicle, it goes with '타다'.

phrases.en: That scientist built a time machine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기나 영화 속에서 기계를 만드는 이야기를 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about building the machine in stories or films.

phrases.en: I like time machine movies a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 타임머신이 나오는 영화를 말해요. '타임머신 이야기'처럼도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A movie featuring a time machine; you can also say '타임머신 이야기'.

explain_en: It pairs with '타다', as in '타임머신을 타다'. When an old photo or object makes you feel you went back in time, people say '타임머신을 탄 것 같아요'.

examples.en: The teacher encouraged the students before their exam.
My friend cheered me up when I was having a hard time.
Encouraging team members is also part of a team leader's job.
We encouraged each other and ran the marathon to the end.
The boss gave words of encouragement to the staff.

examples.ko: 실패한 후배를 격려할 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a way to encourage my junior who failed.

explain: 격려하다는 힘이 빠진 사람에게 용기를 주는 말과 행동이에요. 친구끼리는 '응원하다'를 더 자주 쓰고, 격려하다는 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 하는 느낌이 있어요. '~을/를 격려하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I got encouragement from my teacher and felt strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 격려해 주는 말을 듣는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person being encouraged.

phrases.en: I cheer for my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구끼리는 '격려하다'보다 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more than 격려하다 between friends.

phrases.en: My teacher said encouraging words to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘을 주는 말을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to words that give someone strength.

explain_en: 격려하다 means to give courage to someone who is down. Friends usually say 응원하다 (cheer on), while 격려하다 often sounds like a senior speaking to a junior. It takes an object: '~을/를 격려하다'.

t90.ax: The boss gave words of encouragement to the staff.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 어릴 때부터 제 단짝이에요.
examples.en: That friend has been my best buddy since we were little.
I ended up in the same class as my best friend.
We two are famous at school as a duo.
I fought with my best friend and I feel bad.
I want to meet a close friend at my new school.
A close friend understands you without words.

explain: '단짝'은 늘 둘이 붙어 다니는 사이라서 보통 한 명을 말해요. '베프'는 '베스트 프렌드'를 줄인 젊은 말투이고, '절친'은 '절친한 친구'를 줄인 말이에요.

phrases.en: We quickly became inseparable friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 만나서 매우 친해졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you met and quickly became very close.

phrases.en: She's my bestie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젊은 사람들이 말할 때 쓰는 줄임말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form young people use in casual speech.

phrases.en: We've been close friends since high school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '절친한 친구'의 줄임말로 '단짝'보다 한 사람에 한정되지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Short for 'very close friend'; unlike 'danjjak', it isn't limited to one person.

explain_en: 단짝 is someone you are always with, so it usually points to one person. 베프 is a young-sounding short form of 'best friend', and 절친 is a short form of 절친한 친구 (a very close friend).

examples.en: I feel hurt because no one understands how I feel.
Why don't you recognize my efforts?

examples.ko: 그녀는 남자가 자기 마음을 몰라주는 게 못내 섭섭했어요.
examples.en: She felt sad that the man didn't understand her feelings.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 사정을 몰라줄 때 속상했어요.
examples.en: I was upset when my friend didn't understand my situation.
I hoped he would recognize it, but he never did.

examples.ko: 엄마는 내 고생을 몰라주는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems my mom doesn't appreciate how hard I've worked.

explain: '알아주다'의 반대로, 내 마음이나 노력, 사정을 상대가 이해하거나 인정해 주지 않을 때 써요. 단순히 모르는 게 아니라 '알아줬으면 하는데 안 알아준다'는 서운한 느낌이 들어 있어요.

phrases.en: Nobody recognizes my effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰라주다'와 같은 뜻이지만 조금 더 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 몰라주다, but sounds a bit softer.

phrases.en: My friend doesn't understand how I feel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마음'과 가장 자주 함께 써서 서운한 감정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often paired with 마음 to express hurt feelings.

phrases.en: I resent the person who doesn't understand my feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 사람을 꾸미는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -는 turns it into a phrase that describes a person.

explain_en: It is the opposite of '알아주다', used when someone doesn't understand or acknowledge your feelings, effort or situation. It isn't just not knowing; it carries a hurt feeling of 'I wish you had recognized this, but you didn't'.

examples.en: I had a hard time because of my friend's betrayal.
That movie is a story of love and betrayal.

examples.ko: 가장 믿던 사람의 배반을 겪으면 마음이 무너져요.
examples.en: When the person you trusted most betrays you, your heart breaks.

examples.ko: 회사를 위해 일했는데 돌아온 건 배반이었어요.
examples.en: I worked for the company, and what I got back was betrayal.

examples.ko: 역사책에는 왕에 대한 신하의 배반이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: History books often mention a minister's betrayal of the king.
Betrayal is hard to forgive easily.

explain: '배신'과 뜻이 거의 같아요. '배반'은 믿음이나 약속을 어기고 등을 돌린다는 느낌이 강해서 나라·조직·역사 이야기에도 잘 어울려요. 친구에게 말할 때는 '배신당했어'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I cried a lot because I was betrayed by someone I trusted.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배반'의 피해를 입는 쪽에서 쓰는 말로, 믿은 사람이 등을 돌렸을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the victim's side, when someone you trusted turned against you.

phrases.en: That book tells of the pain of betrayal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 이야기에서 '배반'과 감정을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in writing or stories to pair betrayal with the feeling it causes.

phrases.en: I had a hard time because of my friend's betrayal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배반'과 뜻이 거의 같은데, 일상 대화에서는 '배신'이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, but more natural in everyday conversation.

explain_en: Nearly the same as '배신'. '배반' strongly suggests breaking trust or a promise and turning one's back, so it fits stories about countries, organizations and history. To a friend, '배신당했어' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: Betrayal is hard to forgive easily.

examples.ko: 그 수학자는 오랫동안 어려운 문제를 풀었어요.
examples.en: That mathematician worked on a hard problem for a long time.
My dream is to become a mathematician.
I met a famous mathematician and listened to what they had to say.
The mathematicians gathered and held a meeting.
My uncle is a mathematician, so he loves numbers.
I sent a letter directly to a mathematician.

explain: '-자'는 학문을 하는 사람 뒤에 붙어요. 수학자, 과학자, 철학자처럼요. 학교에서 수학을 가르치는 사람은 '수학 선생님'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I read a book about a famous mathematician.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유명한'을 앞에 붙여 이름이 널리 알려진 수학자를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '유명한' in front describes a mathematician who is widely known.

phrases.en: I want to become a mathematician someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 '-이/가 되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-이/가 되다' when talking about dreams or jobs.

phrases.en: The mathematicians gather and solve the problem together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-들'을 붙이면 여러 명이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-들' means more than one person.

explain_en: The ending '-자' attaches to people who work in a field of study, as in 수학자, 과학자, and 철학자. Someone who teaches math at school is called a '수학 선생님'.

en: to get divorced; to be divorced from; to be separated by divorce

examples.en: My parents divorced when I was little.
I heard that couple decided to divorce.
After the divorce, she started new work.
I asked why they want to divorce.
My friend's parents got divorced and live separately.
I worried about how to live if I divorced.

explain: '이혼하다'는 '~와/과 이혼하다'로 쓰고 결혼한 사이에서만 말해요. 사귀는 사이에서 헤어지는 것은 '헤어지다'예요. 'ㅎ' 때문에 [이호나다]로 소리 나요.

phrases.example: 이혼한 부부도 아이는 같이 키울 수 있어요.
phrases.en: A divorced couple can still raise their child together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이혼하다'를 '-ㄴ'으로 바꿔 사람을 꾸미는 말이에요. 이미 이혼한 사이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This turns the verb into a modifier for a noun. Use it for people who are already divorced.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 요즘 이혼하고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: That person wants to get divorced these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶어 하다'는 다른 사람이 원하는 것을 말할 때 써요. 내가 원하면 '이혼하고 싶어요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-go sipeo hada' describes what another person wants. For yourself, say '이혼하고 싶어요'.

phrases.en: The two of them had a hard time, but they did not get divorced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거의 일을 부정하는 말이에요. 이혼하지 않고 계속 부부로 지낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the negative past form. It means they stayed married.

explain_en: 이혼하다 is used as '~와/과 이혼하다' and only for married couples. For a couple that is dating, use 헤어지다. Because of ㅎ, it is pronounced [이호나다].
